evidence:
other => panic!(
    "unsupported mouse cursor '{other}'; use defer/basic/click/text/crosshair/grab/grabbing/not-allowed or a supported resize cursor"
fix: Stop panicking on app-author input. Add a typed error and return it: `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct UnsupportedMouseCursor(pub String);` (impl Display and Error), change `mouse_cursor_from_name` to return `Result<MouseCursor, UnsupportedMouseCursor>` with `other => Err(UnsupportedMouseCursor(other.to_owned()))`. Also remove the stringly-typed field: `ButtonStyle::mouse_cursor` (line 555) becomes `Option<MouseCursor>`, the builder gains `pub fn try_mouse_cursor(self, cursor: &str) -> Result<Self, UnsupportedMouseCursor>`, and `button.rs:191-200` uses `self.style.mouse_cursor.unwrap_or(...)`. The current path panics at build time when an app writes `ButtonStyle::new().mouse_cursor("bogus")` (button.rs:195 calls this function on the stored string). Material callers that pass theme strings (menus/style.rs, buttons/style.rs, popup.rs:891, controls.rs:241) move to `try_mouse_cursor`. Per CONTRIBUTING, a panicking public function needs a documented contract plus a try_ form; this has neither.

Avoid the two heap allocations per call (to_ascii_lowercase, then replace) by normalising into a stack buffer or comparing without allocating, e.g. `let name = value.trim(); let key = name.bytes().map(|b| if b == b'_' { b'-' } else { b.to_ascii_lowercase() })`, or match on a `[u8; N]` copy when len <= 32 and fall back to the panic-free error path. Lower priority than the panic fix; the function runs once per button build, not per frame.

Either drop `PartialEq` from `ButtonStyle`'s derive list (and the manual impl), or compare by pointer identity so reflexivity holds: `fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool { Rc::ptr_eq(&self.0, &other.0) }`. As written, `style == style` is false whenever a builder is set, which violates the PartialEq contract (x == x).
